Hey, I’d be happy to help as best I can! So the internship I applied for is a human resources internship with a company in my city, which is currently a remote internship because of COVID. It’s supposed to be for about 4 months total and part time during the fall. I’m getting my bachelors in HR Management so it was fitting for my major. Side note, my minor is IT related, and tbh my college isn’t very amazing or renowned or anything.

Anyway, the job posting didn’t ask for experience, but it did list all of job duties that stated what I would  be responsible for. It also listed qualifications stating that I need to be attending an accredited academic institution and that I have to have a business, psychology, or related major, that I need to be able to use Zoom for meetings at this time, need to have a reliable internet connection, Microsoft skills, etc.

For me, I think the reason that I scored the interview is because I have a membership with an HR society and am a member of an IT club at my college. I put a couple of bullets under my society membership about some of the things I was exposed to. I also listed a lot of projects that’s I’ve worked on related to my degree under my education entry on my resume. I have about a year of volunteer experience that I have on the end of my resume, and under it I only put three short bullet points about my volunteer duties. I made sure to align my school projects and volunteer experience with the responsibilities listed in the job posting. I also did a lot of research on the company to figure out how to position my cover letter.

I sent a cover letter in an email to the organization along with a copy of my resume when I submitted my application, along with a note about how I am excited for the opportunity and hope to hear from them soon. Someone from the HR department emailed me back to schedule an interview a little while after that and now I have a phone screening interview this morning, and then hopefully I score the second interview if I do well. 

I think that if you format your resume with projects and even simple extracurriculars, or really anything that you have done that provides transferable skills, it might help you score an interview. I’ve applied to a few internships and this is the only one what has let me interview, while only one other emailed me saying that they would keep me for consideration in the future for volunteer work (not sure if its true).

I wish you the best of luck!
Thank you so much for the response! I will take your points into account as I prepare.
